This guide documents features of R, RStudio, Posit Cloud, and Quarto, which are relevant throughout the course. These can be settings that need to be made or tips that we communicate during the live sessions. 

If you have a request, let us know and we will add guidance here.

## Switch pipe operator

By default, R uses `%>%` as the pipe operator from the `magrittr` package. Since R 4.1.0, the pipe operator is also available as `|>` without loading any packages. The `|>` operator is recommended to be used instead of `%>%`.

To switch to the native pipe operator, follow these steps:

1. Open your project on Posit Cloud
2. On the menu bar of RStudio, click on `Tools` > `Global Options...` (see @fig-global-options)
3. On the left panel, click on `Code`
4. On the right panel, select the 4th check-box from the top next to 'Use native pipe operator, |> (requires R 4.1+) (see @fig-native-pipe)
5. Click on `Apply` and `OK`

```{r}
#| label: fig-global-options
#| fig-cap: RStudio Global Options
#| out-width: 75%
knitr::include_graphics("images/rstudio-tools-global-options.png")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-native-pipe
#| fig-cap: RStudio Code Options
#| out-width: 75%
knitr:::include_graphics("images/rstudio-code-native-pipe.png")
```

## Zotero reference management

We recommend using Zotero as a tool for reference management, but do not teach how to use it in this course. The guidance below will support you in setting up Zotero.

::: {.callout-note}
## Screenshots outdated
The screenshots in this guide are outdated and we are planning to update them by 26th November 2025.
:::

### Get Zotero account

1. Open <https://www.zotero.org/user/login/>
2. Click on Register for a free account
3. Choose username, email, and password
4. Click Register
5. Open your email and verify your account

### Install Zotero desktop client

1. Open <https://www.zotero.org/download/>
2. Download Zotero for your operating system
3. Install Zotero
4. Log in to your Zotero account by opening **Settings -> Sync** and typing the Username and Password you have previously set up
5. Click on the green refresh button in the top-right corner of the Zotero window

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/screenshot-zotero-desktop-client-refresh.png")
```

### Install the Zotero Connector for your browser

1. Open <https://www.zotero.org/download/>
2. Download the Zotero Connector for your browser
3. Install the Zotero Connector
4. Log in to your Zotero account

### Setup Add-ons and the citation key format

1. Go to <https://retorque.re/zotero-better-bibtex/installation/>
2. Click on the latest release so you are redirected to github
3. Find the .xpi file and right-click it. Click on **Save Link As...** and choose your location for saving the file.

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/screenshot-zotero-better-bibtex-addon.png")
```

4. Open **Zotero** -> **Tools** -> **Add-ons** -> (Gear icon) -> **Install Add-on From File...** -> choose the .xpi file you have just saved

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/screenshot-install-betterbibtex-addon.png")
```

5. Restart Zotero

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/screenshot-restart-now.png")
```

6. Wait until the database fully loads. Only the first time is long; the next interactions with Zotero will be much faster.

7. You may need to restart Zotero the second time. Please do so if you see a prompt after Better BibTeX is installed.

8. Go to **Zotero** -> **Settings** -> **Export** -> **Default Format** and change the default format to **Better BibTeX Quick Copy: \cite{citation keys}**

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/screenshot-install-betterbibtex-addon.png")
```

9. In the same setting window, go to **Better BibTeX** -> **Open Better BibTeX preferences...**

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/screenshot-betterbibtex-preferences.png")
```

10. In the **Citation keys** tab, use the following Citation key formula for Better BibTeX: `[auth:lower][year][veryshorttitle1_0:lower]`

The line above means that the citation key will be built from:

- First author's last name in lowercase
- publication year
- The first word from the title in lowercase, not including the connectors such as "the" or "a"

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/screenshot-citation-keys.png")
```

11. Go to **Export** -> **Quick-Copy** in the Better BibTeX preferences. Select **Pandoc citation**.

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/screenshot-pandoc-citation.png")
```


### Change the setting for the citekey autopin delay

1. Open Zotero advanced preferences (**Zotero** -> **Settings** -> **Advanced**)
2. Open the **Config Editor** under the **Advanced Configuration** section

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/screenshot-advanced-config.png")
```

3. Click **I accept the risk!**
4. In the search bar, search for **autopin**

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/screenshot-autopin.png")
```

5. Double-click into the field under **Value**
6. In the new window called **Enter integer value**, change the existing **0** to **2**

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/screenshot-autopin-value-2.png")
```

7. Click **OK**
8. Close all setting windows

## Publish to GitHub Pages

### Navigate to your repository

1. Open github.com in your browser and navigate to the GitHub organisation for the course: <{{< var course.github-org >}}>.

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/gh-pages-01-gh-org.png")
```

2. Use the search field under "Repositories" to find your capstone project repository.

```{r}

```

3. Open your capstone project repository.

```{r}

```

### Make repo public

If your repository's visibility is set to "private" (indicated by a small padlock next to the repositories name), you first need to switch it to "public" by following these steps:

1. Click on "Settings".

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/gh-pages-04-settings.png")
```

2. Stay on "General" and scroll down to the bottom of the page "Danger Zone".

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/gh-pages-05-general.png")
```

3. On the first sub-heading "Change repository visibility", click "Change visibility", then "Change to public".

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/gh-pages-06-danger-zone.png")
```

4. Click "I want to make this repository public".

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/gh-pages-07-public.png")
```

5. Click "I have read and understand these effects".
6. Click "Make this repository public".
7. Provide the requested credentials.
8. Done.

### Publish with GitHub Pages

1. Open your capstone project repository, and click on "Settings".


2. In the left navigation pane, click on "Pages" under "Code and automation".


3. Under "Build and deployment", then under Branch, click the dropdown titled "None".

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/gh-pages-09-dropdown.png")
```

4. In the dropdown, select "main".

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/gh-pages-10-dropdown-main.png")
```

5. Click on the dropdown titled "/ (root)". In the dropdown, select "/docs".

```{r}

```

6. Click "Save".

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/gh-pages-12-save.png")
```

### Edit "About" of repository

1. Open your capstone project repository.

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/gh-pages-13-gear.png")
```

2. On right side, next to "About", click on the gear icon.

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/gh-pages-13-gear-click.png")
```

3. Under "Description" you can add "This project report was prepared for the Data Science for OpenWashData course." or anything else that you would like to highlight.


```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("images/gh-pages-17-about.png")
```

8. Open your published website and enjoy.

## GitHub Copilot Pro subscription

### Get GitHub Copilot Pro

GitHub Copilot is an AI-powered code completion tool that can help you write code faster. GitHub Copilot Pro is available for free to verified teachers and students through GitHub Education.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Free access for students and teachers
Teachers and students can get free access to GitHub Copilot Pro through GitHub Education. Learn more at [GitHub Copilot for Education](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/manage-your-account/get-free-access-to-copilot-pro).
:::

Follow these steps to get GitHub Copilot Pro:

1. Open <https://github.com/settings/copilot> in your browser while logged into your GitHub account.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: GitHub Copilot settings page
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-copilot-settings-page.png")
```

2. If you are eligible for free access through GitHub Education, you will see a message indicating your eligibility. Click on [Get access to GitHub Copilot]{.highlight-yellow}.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Eligibility message and button
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-copilot-eligibility.png")
```

3. If you are not eligible for free access, you can start a free trial or subscribe to GitHub Copilot Pro. Click on [Start free trial]{.highlight-yellow} or [Subscribe]{.highlight-yellow}.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Subscription options
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-copilot-subscription.png")
```

4. Follow the on-screen instructions to complete your subscription or activate your free access.

5. Once activated, you will see a confirmation message.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Confirmation message
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-copilot-activated.png")
```

::: {.callout-important}
## Installing Copilot extensions
After subscribing, you will need to install the GitHub Copilot extension in your code editor (VS Code, RStudio, etc.) to start using it.
:::

### Activate Copilot in RStudio

Once you have subscribed to GitHub Copilot Pro, you can activate it in RStudio to start using AI-powered code completion.

::: {.callout-note}
## RStudio version requirement
GitHub Copilot is available in RStudio version 2023.09.0 or later. If you are using an older version, you will need to update RStudio first.
:::

Follow these steps to activate GitHub Copilot in RStudio:

1. Open RStudio on your computer or in Posit Cloud.

2. On the menu bar, click on [Tools]{.highlight-yellow} > [Global Options...]{.highlight-yellow}.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Tools menu with Global Options
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-rstudio-tools-global-options.png")
```

3. In the left panel, click on [Copilot]{.highlight-yellow}.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Global Options with Copilot in left panel
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-rstudio-copilot-panel.png")
```

4. Check the box next to [Enable GitHub Copilot]{.highlight-yellow}.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Enable GitHub Copilot checkbox
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-rstudio-enable-copilot.png")
```

5. Click [Sign In]{.highlight-yellow} to authenticate with your GitHub account.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Sign In button
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-rstudio-copilot-sign-in.png")
```

6. A browser window will open asking you to authorize RStudio to access GitHub Copilot. Click [Authorize]{.highlight-yellow}.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: GitHub authorization page
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-github-authorize-rstudio.png")
```

7. You will see a confirmation message that GitHub Copilot is now connected. Return to RStudio.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Confirmation message
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-copilot-connected.png")
```

8. Click [Apply]{.highlight-yellow} and [OK]{.highlight-yellow} to save your settings.

9. GitHub Copilot is now active in RStudio. As you type code, you will see AI-powered suggestions appear in gray text. Press [Tab]{.highlight-yellow} to accept a suggestion.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Copilot suggestion in RStudio editor
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-rstudio-copilot-suggestion.png")
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## Using Copilot effectively
- Copilot works best when you provide clear comments or function names describing what you want to accomplish
- You can press `Esc` to dismiss a suggestion you don't want to use
- Try writing a comment like `# Calculate the mean of column x` and see what Copilot suggests
:::

### Cancel GitHub Copilot Pro subscription

If you need to cancel your GitHub Copilot Pro subscription, follow these steps:

1. Open <https://github.com/settings/copilot> in your browser while logged into your GitHub account.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: GitHub Copilot settings page
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-copilot-settings-cancel.png")
```

2. Scroll down to the [Subscription]{.highlight-yellow} section.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Subscription section
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-copilot-subscription-section.png")
```

3. Click on [Manage subscription]{.highlight-yellow} or [Cancel subscription]{.highlight-yellow}.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Manage/Cancel subscription button
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-copilot-cancel-button.png")
```

4. You may be redirected to a billing page. On the billing page, find the GitHub Copilot section and click [Cancel]{.highlight-yellow}.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Billing page with cancel option
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-copilot-billing-cancel.png")
```

5. Confirm your cancellation by following the on-screen prompts.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Cancellation confirmation
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-copilot-cancel-confirm.png")
```

6. You will receive a confirmation that your subscription has been cancelled. You will retain access to GitHub Copilot Pro until the end of your billing period.

```{r}
# Placeholder for screenshot: Final confirmation message
knitr::include_graphics("images/copilot/screenshot-copilot-cancelled.png")
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Free tier users
If you are using GitHub Copilot through GitHub Education, your access will not require cancellation and will remain active as long as you maintain your student or teacher status.
:::
